system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Jinja templating environment for dynamic content
system_prompt_style.note: NPC system prompt is built from the persona/`primary_directive` plus a Jinja templating environment; .npc YAML files supply the directive text. No prompt source file visible in the supplied evidence.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: The `Agent` class in `npcpy` comes with a set of default tools (sh, python, edit_file, web_search, etc.)
env_context_strategy.note: Default Agent explores via sh/python/edit_file tools; team.ctx context text can additionally be injected, and knowledge-graph/vector search is opt-in.

context_compaction.note: No history processor, truncation or summarisation of the message list is described in the README or docs provided.

observation_format.note: Tool results are returned as text entries in the response dict; image/audio/video generation exists but the evidence does not show images being fed back as observations.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: CodingAgent — auto-executes code blocks from LLM responses
tool_call_format.note: Default Agent uses provider tool calling ('Agents with personas, directives, and tool calling'); CodingAgent executes code blocks; jinxes are 'operationalized through a prompt-based flow' for models without tool calling, whose exact syntax is not shown.

tool_count.note: README lists default Agent tools as 'sh, python, edit_file, web_search, etc.' — the 'etc.' means no exact count can be read from the evidence.

edit_primitive.note: An `edit_file` default tool exists but its argument format (search/replace vs rewrite vs line range) is not shown in the supplied evidence.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: Pass Python functions as tools and the agent will call them when relevant:
tool_schema_source.note: Default/custom tools are Python functions with docstrings and type hints (schema derived from the signature); jinxes are hand-written YAML; MCP servers supply further schemas.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: The team's NPCs automatically get access to MCP tools alongside their jinxes.
protocol_standardization.note: Repo topics list mcp, mcp-client, mcp-server; npcpy/mcp_server.py and npcpy/npc2mcp.py ship in the tree.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: A **Jinx** is a multi-step workflow defined as a sequence of steps.
loop_primitives.note: Default Agent.run is a think/act/observe tool-calling loop (react); jinx workflows are fixed pipelines; NPCArray/Sememolution generate competing responses and rank/vote (multi_attempt). Loop code not visible in the evidence.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: The coordinator decides which NPC should handle each part of a request.
planning_granularity.note: No stored plan object is described for the default Agent; routing/planning happens in the coordinator's free-text reasoning. npcpy/work/plan.py exists in the tree but is not documented in the evidence.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: An **NPC** is an AI agent defined by a persona, a model, and optional tools.
multi_agent_topology.note: The coded artifact is the Agent/NPC, which is single. Shipped configuration reaches orchestrator_workers via Team with a forenpc coordinator, and debate via npcpy/mix/debate.py and NPCArray.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: The `Agent` class in `npcpy` comes with a set of default tools (sh, python, edit_file, web_search, etc.)
delegation_mechanism.note: Default Agent tool list contains no delegation tool; a `{{ Jinx('delegate') }}` jinx and 'handling agent passes between NPCs' give role_handoff inside a Team without code changes.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: A human-in-the-loop memory system lets agents learn from interactions, with memories flowing through a review pipeline (pending → approved/rejected/edited).
human_in_loop.note: The documented human gate is review/approval of extracted memories after interactions, not per-action approval; no confirmation policy for tool calls is described.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: Each NPC maintains its own shared context dictionary which serves as working memory during execution.
short_term_state.note: State is messages plus a shared context dictionary carried across jinx steps and team members.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: - Vector database (ChromaDB) for embeddings and semantic search
long_term_memory.note: Also 'SQLite database for conversation history' and 'Knowledge graphs for contextual memory across sessions' (episodic_db), and Skills (SKILL.md jinxes) as a skill library.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: Conversation history, knowledge graphs, and context are persisted between interactions
state_persistence.note: History/context saved to SQLite and re-used between interactions; the evidence does not show a documented full-run resume path for an interrupted agent run.

self_verification.evidence_quote: # Query: sample 10 individuals, generate competing responses, rank them
self_verification.note: Not on for the default Agent: self-critique comes from the debate pattern ('Critique the other approaches') and llm_judge from Sememolution response ranking / memory quality feedback. No harness-run tests or linters documented.

retry_policy.note: No task-level retry policy documented in the supplied README/docs.

rollback.evidence_quote: The `Agent` class in `npcpy` comes with a set of default tools (sh, python, edit_file, web_search, etc.)
rollback.note: No undo/revert/snapshot tool appears in the documented default tool set or elsewhere in the evidence.

termination_condition.note: The evidence does not describe how Agent.run terminates (no max step, token or cost stopping condition shown).

cost_controls.note: Docs mention that 'token usage, and costs are tracked in a conversation_history table' — tracking only; no budget cap, cache or cost-based routing is documented.

timeouts.note: No per-tool or per-run timeout appears in the supplied evidence.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: The `Agent` class in `npcpy` comes with a set of default tools (sh, python, edit_file, web_search, etc.)
execution_isolation.note: npcpy is a pip-installed library whose sh/python tools run on the host; no container or VM sandbox is mentioned anywhere in the evidence.

filesystem_access.note: Relative to the host boundary (G1): tools read/write arbitrary host paths (list_files/read_file examples, edit_file tool); no path allowlist documented.

network_policy.evidence_quote: Parallel Search MCP provides live web search and URL fetching
network_policy.note: web_search tool, remote MCP URLs and provider APIs are reachable; no network restriction option appears in the evidence.

permission_model.evidence_quote: CodingAgent — auto-executes code blocks from LLM responses
permission_model.note: No approval, allowlist or blocklist for actions is documented; code blocks and sh commands are executed directly.

tracing.evidence_quote: Conversations, tool calls, token usage, and costs are tracked in a `conversation_history` table.
tracing.note: Structured per-interaction records in SQLite; a ~/.npcsh/logs/ directory also exists. No OpenTelemetry export mentioned.

replayability.note: No replay of recorded trajectories is described in the supplied evidence.

eval_hooks.note: The Features list and file tree contain fine-tuning, ML functions and unit tests but no benchmark evaluation runner/hook; GSM8k appears only as an example prompt string.

guardrails.evidence_quote: which ensures compliance through software rather than prompts
guardrails.note: Prose-level claim about the Context-Agent-Tool data layer enforcing compliance/least privilege (see the ALARA paper link); no concrete filter or blocklist code is visible in the evidence.

target_domain.evidence_quote: The python library for research and development in NLP, multimodal LLMs, Agents, ML, Knowledge Graphs, and more.
target_domain.note: general_tool_use from MCP/custom tools; swe from CodingAgent and edit_file plus npc-claude/npc-codex launchers; web from web_search and npcpy/work/browser.py; research from the stated purpose.

open_source.note: LICENSE file present in the repo tree; README license badge shows MIT.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: Works with all major LLM providers through LiteLLM

primary_artifact.note: Coded from the pinned repository; associated papers (e.g. ALARA for Agents) are linked but not the coding source.
